projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The stable 14-16 device count confirms full occupancy, while the prolonged zero camera motion strongly suggests the family is gathered in a single area or the cameras are in low-sensitivity mode; this is a benign evening pattern but worth verifying camera configuration if it persists.

The sustained 14-16 device count confirms occupancy, but the complete lack of camera motion during typical evening hours strongly indicates a camera blind spot, system failure, or disabled feeds, leaving the home effectively blind to activity and potential safety or security events.

The consistent 14-15 device count paired with zero camera motion for four hours during typical active hours strongly suggests a camera system failure or presence sensor glitch, creating a critical blind spot for household monitoring and security.

The persistent 14-16 device count alongside zero camera motion or activity for four hours indicates the security cameras are likely offline, in privacy mode, or have motion detection disabled, which could mask security events or indicate a system fault.

Consistently high device count (14-16) over the last 4 hours with zero camera or activity triggers suggests either a highly connected household or potential phantom/ghost devices on the network; worth monitoring for stability.

The household's mobile device count rose from 15 to 16-17 starting at 09:29 AM, with active fluctuations in the last 30 minutes. Given the typical Wednesday school schedule, this pattern strongly suggests a guest has arrived or the children are home, so you may want to verify if you were expecting anyone.

The connected device count increased from 15 to 16 at 09:29, indicating a new device joined the network. Combined with zero camera activity, this suggests a possible visitor, delivery, or returning family member that wasn't captured on video.
The consistent presence of 15 mobile devices from 05:09 through 08:40 AM confirms the entire household is still at home, indicating a later-than-usual Wednesday morning departure for school and work.

The steady rise in connected devices from 14 to 17 between 15:44 and 17:06 aligns with typical after-school arrival times, indicating the children have returned and are settling indoors. This stationary indoor occupancy explains the lack of camera motion triggers, but the complete absence of camera logs alongside high presence confirms the home is occupied while highlighting a potential camera health or privacy mode issue.

Despite a stable presence of 14-16 connected devices and a recent spike to 16, the cameras have logged zero activity in the last 4 hours, suggesting a potential camera system outage, network issue, or privacy mode that is disabling motion detection while the house is actively occupied.
